stories.title: GPT-Realtime-2 Model Announcement
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
OpenAI updated its WebRTC-based Realtime API with a new model variant, and Simon Willison's open-source WebRTC audio session tool has been updated to support document context — meaning you can now pass text documents into a live audio session.

↳ THE REAL STORY
The document context addition is the practical change here. Previously, the WebRTC realtime tool was essentially a voice interface to a stateless model. Adding document context means developers can now feed in a reference file — a spec, a transcript, a knowledge base chunk — and have the audio model reason against it in real time. For anyone building voice assistants that need to stay grounded in specific content (support docs, meeting notes, product manuals), this closes a gap that previously required awkward workarounds like pre-stuffing system prompts manually.
stories.considerations: The excerpt is truncated and sourced from Simon Willison's personal tooling blog, not an official OpenAI product announcement. It's unclear from the available text what 'GPT-Realtime-2' actually refers to — whether it's a formally named model, an internal version bump, or just a label applied to whatever model the updated API now routes to. Before building on assumptions about model capabilities or pricing, check the OpenAI API changelog directly. The signal here is thin.

stories.title: AI Economics for Dummies
stories.summary:
↳ WHAT'S NEW
McSweeney's published a satire piece on AI economics, using a crematorium-and-propane circular money loop to illustrate how AI infrastructure investment rounds get reported as revenue.

↳ THE REAL STORY
The joke lands because the underlying accounting is real: hyperscaler cloud commitments between AI labs and their investors routinely get counted as revenue on both sides of the ledger. Microsoft invests in OpenAI; OpenAI buys Azure compute; Microsoft books it as cloud revenue. The circularity is not hidden — it is in the footnotes — but it rarely makes the headline numbers.
stories.considerations:
↳ WORTH WATCHING
Satire is doing the work that financial journalism mostly isn't. When a McSweeney's bit is a more accurate description of AI capital flows than the average earnings call summary, that is worth sitting with. The open question is when — not if — a major analyst or regulator starts treating these circular commitments as related-party transactions requiring separate disclosure. That reclassification, if it comes, would reprice several balance sheets overnight.
